Definition: to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger)
BiblicalUsage: Nahak means to bray like an ass or to scream from hunger, and it is used for the complaints of the empty. In Job 6:5 Job asks if the wild ass brays when he has grass, or the ox lows over his fodder, and in Job 30:7 the outcasts bray among the bushes and gather under the nettles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Job's point is simple: a creature cries out because it lacks something, and so does a man; the bray is not the problem; the hunger behind it is.
